title: Split continuous-batcher state machine and add lock-free KV shard read path
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Problem: The continuous batching executor and the KV cache share a tightly coupled state machine and use coarse-grained locks in the hot read path. This causes p99 latency spikes under multi-tenant bursts and prevents us from fully leveraging per-shard parallelism. It also makes incremental refactors high-risk because the batching state and cache invariants are interleaved.

Goal: Decouple the continuous-batcher control flow from KV cache lifecycle, introduce a lock-free read path for cache lookups (RCU-style), and simplify the executor state transitions so we can reason about and test them independently. This should reduce tail latency, improve throughput under bursty workloads, and unblock future batching optimizations (multi-lane coalescing, per-tenant QoS).

Scope:
- Extract batching state machine into a small deterministic state enum and a single-threaded coordinator component.
- Implement a read-mostly lock-free KV shard view using epoch-based reclamation (RCU) and atomics for pointer swaps. Writes/evictions will go through a reconciler thread that publishes new shard views.
- Replace existing mutex-protected hot-path lookups with the new read path; keep fallback to mutex while flagged via runtime config.
- Upgrade dependencies required for safe RCU and concurrency improvements (crossbeam-epoch -> latest, tokio -> 1.30.x), and audit unsafe blocks.
- Add microbench harnesses and end-to-end latency benchmarks, including multi-tenant synthetic traces and real production trace replay (sanitized).

Planned deliverables:
- Small, well-documented state machine crate (batch-state) with unit tests and a verification matrix.
- lockfree-kv-shard module with RCU publish/subscribe API and eviction reconciler.
- Feature-flagged rollout plan and migration patch for canary testing.
- Benchmark report with end-to-end p50/p95/p99 before/after and a dashboard panel for rollout watch.

Expected outcome:
- ~10-18% reduction in p99 generation latency on mixed workloads observed in internal benchmarks.
- 15-30% throughput improvement for long-history KV-heavy prompts due to reduced contention.
- Easier-to-review, smaller follow-up PRs for batching optimizations.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- RCU-style approach increases memory use transiently because old shard snapshots are retained until reclamation. We'll bound retention with shard-level epoch windows and quota per-shard.
- More complex release process: the feature flag and fallback path are mandatory to mitigate stability risks.
- Upgrading tokio and crossbeam requires coordinated changes in several crates; plan to stage these as separate dependency bump PRs prior to main refactor merge.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge batch-state crate behind a feature flag and run unit/integration tests.
2) Merge lockfree-kv-shard behind another flag; run microbenchmarks in CI.
3) Canary deploy to internal dev environment with 10% of traffic; monitor cost/latency and KV hit rates.
4) Gradually increase to 50% with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and manual sign-off.

Metrics to watch during canary:
- p99 and p50 latency for generation route by tenant tier
- KV cache hit ratio and stale shard read rate
- Allocation churn and RSS per worker process
- Rate of failing lookups or eviction errors
- Request error budget consumption and CPU load per GPU host

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions with exhaustive coverage of edge cases (interrupts, early flushes).
- Fault-injection tests that simulate reconciler crashes and slow reclamation.
- Benchmarks: local microbench (single-host), simulated cluster using production trace replay, and a small-scale canary.

Observability additions:
- New metrics: batch_state_transitions_total, kv_shard_publish_duration_ms, kv_lockfree_reads_total, kv_pending_snapshots, kv_reclamation_pause_ms.
- Dashboard: batch-state health panel and a kv-shard memory dashboard.
- Alert: kv_shard_pending_snapshots > 100 for 5m or kv_reclamation_pause_ms > 200ms.

Security and compliance: no customer data changes anticipated. Ensure KMS/HSM call sites remain isolated; confirm no secrets are copied into shard snapshots.

Documentation: add design doc in Confluence (link below), inline crate docs, and a short migration guide for infra/ops.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RN/Lockfree-KV-Shard-and-Batch-State-Design
- PR draft (batch-state): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891
- PR draft (lockfree-kv-shard): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
- Benchmark results (initial): https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/lockfree-kv-shard/2026-01-28
- Canary run dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/lockfree-canary-2026

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle memory safety bugs in epoch-based reclamation. Mitigation: incremental merge, heavy unit tests, fuzzing on unsafe code, and core review by two senior engineers.
- Risk: regression in latency for short prompts due to publish pauses. Mitigation: tune reconciler rate and fallback to mutex-protected path under load.
- Risk: dependency bumps cause unrelated breakages. Mitigation: staged dependency PRs with compatibility tests and shrinkwrap CI.

Next steps (short-term):
- Split out dependency bump PRs (crossbeam, tokio) and get them green in CI (owner: Diego).
- Submit initial batch-state crate PR for review (owner: Arielle).
- Build microbench harness and run baseline (owner: Sita Rao).
